messages:
sam: Heads-up — finance flagged a bunch of requests from an OEM partner being charged to our infra project. Seems correlated with large batched SDK calls. noticed at 07:42 UTC.

emily: any logs? could be header trimming in the SDK or an auth race.

derek: pulling traces now. interesting: many requests arrive with X-Redwood-Origin present but routed_project still fallback. sample: `ts=2025-05-18 auth=ok origin=Xr-Org:123 header_present=true claims_project= - routed_project=infra-main`

nina: that suggests routing decided before origin header was applied. We shipped an async fast-path that parallelizes header enrichment and token introspect last sprint. maybe routing uses token introspect result when it returns first.

sam: what are mitigations? We can't bill partners incorrectly. options: 1) force synchronous enrichment (safer, slower), 2) change fallback to charge central-billing for unattributed for 24h, 3) fail when origin absent, 4) prefer header if present regardless of token introspect timing.

emily: prefer 2 short-term to avoid customer impact. 1 is the real fix but risks latency regressions for high-frequency clients.

derek: agree with 2 + quick canary for synchronous enrichment on low-traffic route to measure latency impact. Also emit telemetry: `auth.attribution_source` and `routing.decision_latency_ms`.

ops-bot: alert: billing-attribution-anomaly threshold crossed (5m avg >3%). Paging eng-platform.

sam: rollout plan: set unattributed_default=central-billing-pool, enable 100% sampling on attribution traces for 15m, and schedule a canary to test sync-enrichment on 5% traffic.

emily: adding console UX: small indicator on Key details page showing "last 24h attribution: X% missing" and a link for support refund request. Product okayed.

derek: will add a dashboard tile for routing.decision_latency_ms and histogram of enrichment_time (header vs token). Also add an alert if `auth.attribution_source=fallback` > 1% for 10m.

sam: canary patch: flip flag auth.sync_enrich=false -> true for canary; target 5% traffic. deploy command: `curl -s -XPOST https://deploy.internal/trigger -d 'service=auth-router&flag=sync_enrich&value=true&target=canary'`

deploy-bot: deploy started: auth-router v3.6.0-canary -> 5% traffic. CI ok.

ops-bot: sampling increased for attribution traces to 100% for 15m.

emily: canary results after 8m: latency p95 for auth-router increased 6ms on cold paths, enrichment success up from 94% -> 99.2%, fallback routing down to baseline. promoting to 20% to gather more numbers.

derek: data looks promising. raising rollout to 50% with a staged plan. Also pushed telemetry PR with `auth.attribution_source` enum values ["header","claims","fallback"] and `billing.attributed` boolean.

sam: follow-ups: (A) retro on async enrichment tradeoffs and perf budget (B) telemetry/dashboards (derek) (C) console key indicator + refund flow (emily) (D) liaise with finance on central-billing window (nina).

emily: small UX note: make the key indicator non-blocking and clickable to open refund request modal. keeping banner subtle.

sam: thanks team. good work catching this quickly. we'll reassess default fallback policy next week. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: incident mitigated — central billing default applied and sync-enrich canary healthy. Monitoring for 24h.
